deck.audience: ML researchers and graduate students interested in LLM-based agents and planning systems

brief.title: KnowSelf: Teaching LLM Agents When to Think, Reflect, or Seek Knowledge
brief.one_liner: KnowSelf introduces agentic knowledgeable self-awareness, enabling LLM agents to autonomously decide when to act directly, self-reflect, or consult external knowledge during planning tasks.
brief.goal: The audience should understand the problem of indiscriminate knowledge injection in agent planning, how KnowSelf's three-situation framework (fast/slow/knowledgeable thinking) addresses it, and the empirical evidence showing KnowSelf outperforms strong baselines while using minimal external knowledge.

slides.title: KnowSelf: Agentic Knowledgeable Self-Awareness for LLM-Based Agents
slides.objective: Cover slide with paper title, source reference (arxiv.org/abs/2504.03553), and key tagline about enabling agents to autonomously regulate knowledge utilization through situational self-awareness.

slides.title: Current Agent Training Uses 'Flood Irrigation' — Indiscriminate Knowledge Injection Hurts Efficiency
slides.objective: Present the core problem: existing approaches blindly inject gold trajectories, external feedback, and domain knowledge without considering situational needs. Contrast with human self-awareness in decision-making. Use a conceptual diagram or bullet-point comparison of three existing paradigms (trajectory imitation, trial-and-error, knowledge-augmented) and their limitations.

slides.title: Three Situational Modes: Fast Thinking, Slow Thinking, and Knowledgeable Thinking
slides.objective: Define the three cognitive situations that KnowSelf identifies. Show the decision criterion: fast thinking (direct correct action), slow thinking (correct after reflection), knowledgeable thinking (needs external knowledge). Use a flow diagram or decision tree visualization referencing the framework figure.

slides.title: KnowSelf Framework: Data Construction → Two-Stage Training → Self-Aware Inference
slides.objective: Walk through the three-step pipeline: (1) heuristic situation judgment to mark special tokens on self-explored trajectories, (2) SFT followed by RPO training, (3) inference with selective token generation triggering reflection or knowledge retrieval. Reference the framework figure (figure_3.jpg).

slides.title: KnowSelf Correctly Heats a Mug and Places a Saltshaker Where Baselines Fail
slides.objective: Show two qualitative task examples side-by-side: (a) 'put a hot mug in cabinet' where KnowSelf uses reflection to heat the mug while OpenAI-O1 fails, and (b) 'put a saltshaker in drawer' where KnowSelf applies knowledge to place the object while DeepSeek-R1 gets stuck. Reference figure_1.jpg.

slides.title: KnowSelf Achieves 84.33% on ALFWorld with Llama-8B Using Only 15% Knowledge
slides.objective: Present the main results table comparing KnowSelf against ReAct, Reflexion, ExpeL, ETO, KnowAgent, and WKM across GPT-4o, Llama-8B, and Gemma-2B backbones on six ALFWorld task types. Highlight that KnowSelf uses far less knowledge (15% and 26%) yet outperforms methods using 100% knowledge. Use a data table visualization.

slides.title: Minimal Knowledge, Maximum Impact: KnowSelf's Efficiency Advantage Over Full-Knowledge Methods
slides.objective: Emphasize the efficiency angle: KnowSelf uses only ~15-26% knowledge queries compared to 100% for KnowAgent/WKM/ExpeL, yet achieves the best overall scores. Show a comparative bar chart or highlight the Know% column against All accuracy. Discuss the scaling behavior across model sizes (Gemma-2B vs Llama-8B).

slides.title: Key Takeaways: Self-Awareness Is the Missing Piece in Agent Planning
slides.objective: Summarize 5 key findings: (1) Indiscriminate knowledge injection is wasteful and suboptimal, (2) Agents can learn situational self-awareness via special tokens with lightweight heuristic labeling, (3) KnowSelf with Llama-8B outperforms strong baselines including GPT-4o ReAct (84.33% vs 76.12%) and GPT-4o ExpeL (79.85%), (4) Only 15-26% knowledge usage needed versus 100% for competing methods, (5) The paradigm generalizes across model scales — even Gemma-2B reaches 79.85% matching GPT-4o ExpeL.
